The shooting vest

The shooting vest is the most visible part of a shooter's gear. It is not about fashion: the vest keeps cartridges at hand, protects the shoulder from recoil and helps you mount the gun the same way each time.

Pockets are the heart of a vest. There are usually two large front pockets for cartridges, left and right, so you can load with either hand. Often there is a separate pocket or mesh bag for empty cases, and small pockets for chokes, a choke key and earplugs. Cartridges must not fall out when you bend down.

On the shoulder there is a shoulder pad, a smooth insert of softer or firmer material. The stock sits on it: the smooth surface does not snag on the fabric during the mount, and the padding softens recoil a little. The pad must be on the shoulder you shoot from, and many vests have one on both sides.

For Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the vest carries a contrasting horizontal line 25 cm below the shoulder axis and parallel to it. Before you call for the target, and until the target appears, the top of the stock must stay below it, and the referee checks this. In Compak® Sporting there is no such line, because the gun position at the call is free.

Tip: Many vests are sold with the line already sewn on; if not, you can sew or stick one on. If you plan to shoot both disciplines, choose a vest with the line: it works everywhere.

Vests come in different cuts, including cuts made for women, which allow for the chest and narrower shoulders. When the vest fits, the pad sits exactly where the stock goes and does not get in the way of the mount. In a vest that does not fit, the stock may catch on the fabric or seams.

How to choose your first vest: it should fit loosely but not flap, so try it on over the clothes you will shoot in. Mount an empty, checked gun, or at least copy the movement with your arms: the fabric must not bunch up and catch the stock. Summer vests have a mesh back; heavier ones are for the cold. In both disciplines a vest may not be worn over a bare chest.

Key points

  • A vest keeps cartridges at hand, protects the shoulder and helps a consistent mount.
  • A vest cut for your build puts the shoulder pad in the right place.
  • The shoulder pad goes on the shoulder you shoot from.
  • Sporting™ needs a contrasting line 25 cm below the shoulder axis and parallel to it; Compak® Sporting does not.
  • Try the vest on over your shooting clothes; do not wear it over a bare chest.

Did you know?

Vests often have pads on both shoulders, because many shooters are left-handed or shoot from the left shoulder because of their master eye.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Where must the contrasting line be on a Sporting™ vest?

    1. At the level of the belt
    2. 25 cm below the shoulder axis
    3. Across the middle of the back
    4. Along the edge of the pocket
    Answer

    25 cm below the shoulder axis

    The Sporting™ rules require a line 25 cm below the shoulder axis and parallel to it.

    Chapter 3 · The 25 cm marking line on the jacket

  2. What is the shoulder pad on a vest for?

    1. So the stock slides into place smoothly
    2. To carry spare chokes and a key
    3. To show the shooter's number
    4. To keep the vest warm in winter
    Answer

    So the stock slides into place smoothly

    A smooth pad helps a clean mount and absorbs a little recoil.

  3. Do the Compak® Sporting rules require a jacket line?

    1. Yes, exactly as in Sporting™
    2. Yes, but only for junior shooters
    3. No: the gun position at the call is free
    4. Only at world championships
    Answer

    No: the gun position at the call is free

    In Compak® Sporting the gun may already be mounted before the call, so no line is required.

    Chapter 17 · Gun position when calling
